chemicals.name: Ammonia, Anhydrous
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Dense toxic alkaline gas cloud hugging ground despite lower nominal vapor density due to aerosolization; severe chemical pneumonitis and fatal pulmonary edema.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Do NOT apply water into liquid ammonia pools. Use high-capacity water fog curtains downwind to knock down ammonia vapor clouds without contacting the leak source.

chemicals.name: Chlorine
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Extremely heavy corrosive suffocating gas cloud flowing into low-lying depressions and valleys; acute asphyxiation and severe lung tissue destruction.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Wear Level A fully encapsulated HazMat suit. Never spray water on a leaking container (water + chlorine forms highly corrosive hypochlorous and hydrochloric acids). Apply water spray curtains downwind.

chemicals.name: Benzene
chemicals.hazard_class: Class 3 (Flammable Liquid, Toxic, Known Human Carcinogen)
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Vapor cloud explosion (VCE), BLEVE risk for pressurized storage tanks, severe hematological toxicity and chronic leukemia induction.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Aqueous Film-Forming Foam (AFFF), Alcohol-Resistant AFFF. High-volume deluge water spray on unignited storage tanks to prevent boiling expansion.

chemicals.name: Styrene Monomer, Stabilized
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Uncontrolled runaway exothermic polymerization (LG Polymers Vizag 2020 accident scenario); self-accelerating thermal decomposition rupturing tanks and spreading toxic neurotoxic monomer vapors.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Continuous refrigeration and tertiary-butylcatechol (TBC) inhibitor injection. AR-AFFF foam blanket; heavy water deluge for exterior tank shell cooling.

chemicals.name: Hydrogen Sulfide
chemicals.physical_state: Colorless Gas (Rotten Egg Odor at low ppm; paralyzes olfactory nerve immediately at >100 ppm)
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Instant knockdown and respiratory arrest at concentrations >= 500 ppm ('knockdown gas'). Flammable and explosive in air (LEL 4.3%, UEL 46%).
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Do NOT extinguish burning gas unless leak can be shut off immediately. Combustion converts H2S into SO2 (less immediately lethal than raw H2S).

chemicals.name: Vinyl Chloride, Stabilized
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Catastrophic tank BLEVE, heavy ground-hugging vapor cloud, severe hepatic angiosarcoma carcinogen, toxic combustion into Phosgene (COCl2).
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Unmanned monitor water deluge to cool tanks. If involved in fire, toxic phosgene gas is produced; full SCBA Level A mandatory.

chemicals.name: Ethylene Oxide
chemicals.hazard_class: Class 2.3 (Poison Gas, Inhalation Hazard / Extremely Flammable)
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Explosive decomposition even in total absence of air/oxygen; severe pulmonary edema and mutagenic/carcinogenic devastation.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Massive deluge with water spray. Tanks may explode violently when heated due to internal runaway chain decomposition.

chemicals.name: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG - Propane / Butane)
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: BLEVE fireball with thermal radiation lethal at 500m; vapor cloud explosion travelling long distances along ground.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Apply massive water streams to tank shell sides from unmanned monitors. If water cannot be sustained, evacuate radius of at least 1 mile (1600m).

chemicals.name: Sulfur Dioxide
chemicals.physical_state: Colorless Liquefied Compressed Gas (Choking Pungent Odor)
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Forms sulfurous acid (H2SO3) upon contact with moist mucous membranes; acute bronchospasm, chemical laryngospasm, and permanent lung damage.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Water spray curtain to absorb toxic SO2 vapors. Do not direct water directly into liquid SO2 pools.

chemicals.name: Ammonium Nitrate, Solid
chemicals.primary_disaster_risk: Catastrophic supersonic detonation (Beirut Port 2020 / Texas City scenario) when exposed to heat or organic contamination; massive shockwave and toxic red-orange nitrogen dioxide (NO2) plume.
chemicals.firefighting_protocol: Douse with massive volumes of water from distant unmanned monitors immediately. Do NOT fight fire if fire reaches nitrate mass or if smoke turns reddish-brown.
